rv.q: Still, though the whole doesn’t quite pay off emotionally, the individual parts often have intelligent and clever elements that go beyond mere riffing on sci-fi scenarios, and the actors move with panache between the scenes.

Florida is certainly no stranger to genre writing (their work has appeared in such exalted publications as 2000 AD and Heavy Metal ), but they've yet to find a way to form a happy union between their love of science fiction and their ambitions within the medium of theater.
Choppy and uneven, “Radical Futures” is a hodgepodge that lacks cohesion.

cn.t: Critics find "Radical Futures" uneven but charming—its sci-fi anthology structure earns praise for ambition, while cohesion remains a nagging issue. Frederickson and Stevens win points; the script doesn't always.
